title: Visualizable Graph Payload
description: Rich, domain-agnostic graph payload contract for shared visualization rendering.

graph_kind.description: Optional domain hint (for UI text and filtering, not required for layout).

graph_id.description: Optional stable identifier for the rendered graph artifact.

render_modes.description: Optional named modes enabled by the wrapper (e.g., flowchart, architecture).

presentation_nodes.description: First-class presentation-only nodes that reference canonical root entities without changing graph semantics.

renderer_dependencies.description: Ordered optional renderer capabilities resolved through the renderer-owned trusted dependency registry.

categories.description: Optional machine-readable category catalog for legend/filtering.

edge_categories.description: Optional machine-readable edge-category catalog for legend/filtering.

detail_levels.description: Ordered cumulative visibility levels from coarsest to finest.

label.description: Reader-facing name shown in the detail control.

description.description: One sentence describing what this level reveals.

detailLevel.description: A named verbosity step the viewer offers for inspector content, letting a reader move between summary and full detail.

rendererDependency.description: A runtime capability the payload needs in order to render, such as MathJax for TeX. Only registered trusted loaders are honoured; unknown dependency ids are rejected rather than fetched.

version.description: MathJax major version. Only `3` is supported.

macros.description: Self-contained MathJax macro definitions. Strings and replacement-first arrays `[replacement, argument_count]` or `[replacement, argument_count, optional_default]` are canonical; integer-first arrays remain accepted for legacy schema-v2 payloads.

configuration.description: MathJax TeX input configuration, including the payload's complete `macros` mapping.

mathjaxDependency.description: Declares that the self-contained payload contains TeX requiring MathJax. The renderer normalizes every schema-supported macro tuple at its browser boundary; commands the pinned runtime cannot resolve are reported without a document-specific command catalog.

documentMeta.description: Optional document-level context shown in viewer metadata.

selectable.description: Whether a reader can select this node.

inspectable.description: Whether selecting it opens inspector content.

draggable.description: `none` to pin it, `self` to move only the group, `members` to carry its members along.

collapse_effect.description: `self` to allow collapsing into a single cell, `none` to keep it always expanded. Container collapse rolls endpoints up to visible owners and never invokes node-omission composition.

presentationNodeInteraction.description: Which interactions a presentation node supports. Stated explicitly rather than inferred, so a grouping meant only as a backdrop cannot be selected or dragged by accident.

id.description: Unique identifier, distinct from every entity id.

type.description: Category naming this presentation node's class, resolved against `categories`.

short_title.description: Title drawn in the node cell.

position.description: Ordering position, on the same scale as entity positions.

description.description: One-sentence summary shown in the inspector.

ref.description: Document-assigned number, drawn as the subtitle alongside the type.

details.description: Extractor-selected inspector sections, using the same generic format as entities.

member_ids.description: Ids of the nodes this presentation node covers. Members may belong to more than one presentation node.

presentationNode.description: A node that groups other nodes for presentation rather than representing a distinct object of the domain. It carries the same identity and inspector fields as an entity, plus the members it covers. Memberships may overlap, and the renderer owns their layout, selection, drag, hide, collapse, and persistence independently of the members.

label.description: Reader-facing name shown in the selector.

activation.description: `all` when every listed node must be present to offer the facet; `multiple` when two or more suffice.

presentationNodeFacet.description: One selectable grouping within a presentation-node control: a named set of nodes a reader can bring into view together.

selector_label.description: Prompt shown on the selector itself.

default_facet.description: Facet active on load, or null to start with none applied.

presentationNodeControl.description: A reader-facing selector that switches between presentation-node facets, letting one graph offer several alternative groupings of the same nodes.

line_pattern.description: Stroke pattern for the edge path.

stroke_width.description: Stroke width in user units, overriding the resolved base width.

edgePresentationStyle.description: Paint overrides a presentation variant may apply to an edge. Only these three keys are honoured; arbitrary CSS and expressions are rejected.

id.description: Identifier for this variant, unique within its facet. Participates in projection and bundling keys so visually distinct edges are never merged.

equals.description: Scalar the facet's field must equal for this variant to apply. Matching is strict equality, so booleans, strings and numbers do not cross-match.

label.description: Short reader-facing name shown in the Edge presentation legend.

description.description: One sentence telling a reader what this variant means about the dependency.

style.description: Paint applied to edges matching this variant.

edgePresentationVariant.description: One value of a presentation facet: the scalar an edge field must equal, and the paint applied when it does. Variants appear in the Edge presentation legend, so label and description are reader-facing.

id.description: Identifier for this facet, unique within edge_presentation, and the legend grouping it appears under.

label.description: Short reader-facing name for the distinction this facet draws.

field.description: Scalar edge property to read: an authored property such as `implicit`, the renderer-set `derived` flag marking an edge composed across omitted nodes, or a one-level metadata key such as `metadata.provenance`. Nested paths beyond one metadata level are not resolved.

variants.description: Values of the field and the paint each receives. A field value matching no variant is left unstyled by this facet.

edgePresentationFacet.description: A declarative mapping from one scalar edge field to styled variants. This is how a graph expresses a visual distinction WITHOUT inventing a new edge type: keep the edge vocabulary closed and vary a field instead. Facets are applied generically by the renderer, so adding one is a payload change requiring no renderer code. Semantic style is applied first, declared variants second, computed overlays last; multiple facets compose, later variants merging over earlier ones.

uiConfig.description: Optional renderer-level preferences. Missing fields fall back to renderer defaults.

edge_presentation.description: Payload-declared scalar-equality facets that add bounded presentation styles without changing edge semantics.

aspect_ratio.description: Best-effort target width-to-height ratio for packing disconnected layout components.

collapsed_containers.description: Container ids initially shown without their descendants.

detail_level.description: Initially selected id from the ordered top-level detail_levels catalog.

type_styles.description: Optional renderer styles for node types.

edge_styles.description: Optional renderer styles for edge types.

edge_metadata_styles.description: Optional labels, explanations, and bounded style overrides for generic renderer-computed edge metadata states. Hidden-detail summaries use a halo, same-type multiplicity uses width, and mixed types use constituent-color gradients with neutral outlines.

subsumptions.description: Acyclic information order over relation types. At a visible endpoint a stronger eligible result suppresses weaker equivalents; incomparable results stay bundled. Distinct from category parents, which are filter hierarchy only and never imply substitutability.

transformations.description: How relations compose when the graph is projected.

relationSemantics.description: Domain meaning of this graph's relations, supplied by the adapter. The renderer owns the projection algorithm; this object owns what those projections are allowed to mean. Omitting it is valid and means the renderer derives nothing: hiding an intermediate node then removes its edges without substituting any derived dependency.

node_omission.description: How a path through an omitted node composes into a derived edge.

relationTransformations.description: Declared transformations the renderer may apply while projecting a graph.

rules.description: Finite rule set forming a relation transducer. Rules are applied finitely, self-links are rejected, equivalent witnesses are deduplicated, a derived edge is never composed again, and a matching direct edge always takes precedence.

nodeOmissionTransformation.description: Composition rules used when a node is hidden and its incoming and outgoing edges would otherwise both disappear. Without a matching rule the renderer derives nothing, so a graph that wants reachability preserved across hidden nodes must declare the compositions it considers truthful. Container collapse does not use this: it rolls endpoints up to visible owners instead.

id.description: Identifier for this rule, used in derived-edge provenance so a reader can see why an edge was drawn.

causes.description: Omission causes this rule applies to, distinguishing for example a node hidden by a reader from one removed by a filter.

left_types.description: Relation types of the incoming edge, arriving at the omitted node.

right_types.description: Relation types of the outgoing edge, leaving the omitted node.

outcomes.description: Derived relations this composition may truthfully produce.

relationTransformationRule.description: One composition: when an edge of a left type meets an edge of a right type at an omitted node, the derived edge may take any declared outcome type. Every outcome must be independently true of the composed path, not merely plausible.

type.description: Relation type of the derived edge. Must name a declared edge category, which keeps the vocabulary closed under composition.

fidelity.description: `exact` when the composition preserves the original information; `degraded` when the derived edge is weaker than the path it replaces. The renderer may present degraded results differently.

relationOutcome.description: A derived relation and how much information survived producing it.

weaker_types.description: Relation types suppressed in its presence at that endpoint.

relationSubsumption.description: One step of the information order: a stronger relation type and the weaker types it suppresses when both reach the same visible endpoint.

id.description: Identifier referenced by an entity `type` or an edge `type`.

label.description: Reader-facing name shown in the legend.

shape.description: Node outline for this category. Ignored for edge categories.

description.description: One sentence telling a reader what belongs in this category.

parent.description: Identifier of the enclosing category, when this one refines another.

color.description: Category colour as a CSS hex string.

category.description: A node or edge class the viewer can style, filter, and list in the legend. Categories form a shallow tree via `parent`, and hiding a parent hides its children. An edge whose type names no category fails validation, which is what keeps the vocabulary closed.

description.description: One clause naming how the source is used by the target. Shown to a reader on hover, so it carries the meaning a type value would otherwise encode.

details.description: Extractor-selected inspector content, rendered without domain inference.

confidence.description: How firmly the source establishes this dependency.

implicit.description: True when the dependency is inferred from the argument rather than asserted by the document. The default provenance facet keys on this field.

evidence.description: Smallest source passage or location supporting the dependency.

label.description: Optional short text drawn on the edge itself.

edge_label.description: Alternative edge caption used where `label` is reserved for another purpose.

source.description: Provenance of the edge record itself, distinct from `implicit`, which describes the dependency.

metadata.description: Structured detail with no presentation meaning of its own. A facet may key on a one-level key here via `metadata.<key>`.

weight.description: Relative strength or multiplicity, used by layout rather than semantics.

phase.description: Extractor-defined stage or pass this edge originated from.

projection_target.description: Identifier this edge is redirected to when a projection collapses its endpoint.

edgeCommon.description: Fields any edge may carry in addition to its endpoints and type. The edge vocabulary is intentionally small, so the specific character of a dependency belongs in `description` and `metadata` rather than in a new type; presentation facets can then key on those fields to draw the distinction visually.

edgeCanonical.description: An edge as authored in the payload, carrying its endpoints and type alongside the common edge fields. Canonical edges are the only ones projection traverses; derived edges are produced by the renderer and are never re-composed.

entity.description: A render node and its metadata.

type.description: Renderer category/type used for legend, style, and filtering.

kind.description: Optional open-ended semantic kind used for color assignment independently of node shape.

detail_level.description: Id from the ordered top-level detail_levels catalog. The entity is visible when this level or any finer level is selected.

label.description: Optional display label for this node. Renderers should fall back to short_title.

details.description: Optional extractor-selected inspector content rendered without domain inference.

container.description: Canonical id of this entity's single structural parent.

decorations.description: Optional domain-neutral visual annotations attached to the node rather than represented as graph edges.

type.description: Generic decoration family, such as outline or badge.

style.description: Generic rendering style within the decoration family.

references.description: Canonical ids whose relationship is summarized by the decoration.

presentation.description: Optional domain-neutral visual role used consistently by graph nodes and legend entries.

form.description: Whether the entity is presented as an ordinary node or a framed containment region.

tone.description: Relative visual intensity without prescribing a domain-specific color.

children.description: Deprecated inverse containment field; use container on each child.

tex_label.description: The TeX \label key on this object's statement, recorded verbatim. Extractors read it off the source without inference; a renderer may resolve it to the number the document prints.
